subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Endowment Effect
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Endowment Effect.

hook.text: Students given mugs demanded $7 to sell them. Students without mugs offered only $3 to buy. Same mug.

buildup.text: Thaler's experiments showed that owning something instantly increases its perceived value.

discovery.text: The endowment effect: we overvalue what we own because selling feels like a loss, not a neutral exchange.

twist.text: Experienced traders show reduced endowment effects. Treating items as fungible weakens the emotional ownership.

climax.text: Before refusing to sell, ask: would I buy this at the price I'm demanding? If not, your valuation is biased.

punchline.text: Owning it doesn't make it worth more.

quiz.question: What causes the endowment effect?
options: Objects genuinely increase in value when owned
Selling feels like a loss, inflating perceived value
